Prime Minister shares an article highlighting India’s growing focus on skill development and making skilling a preferred career pathway
articles.full_content:
The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, today shared an article by Union Minister of State Shri Jayant Chaudhary, highlighting the country's growing focus on skill development and the importance of making skilling a preferred career pathway.
Shri Chaudhary highlighted the upcoming WorldSkills Asia 2027, the PM-SETU initiative to upgrade ITIs, and efforts to strengthen industry-linked training, reflecting on how these initiatives are preparing youth for emerging opportunities in the age of AI.
The Prime Minister's Office posted on X:
“India is taking its skilling journey to the world stage!

Central Government Approves ₹10,600 Crore Production Linked Incentive Scheme to Strengthen Technical Textiles Sector: Union Minister of Textiles Shri Giriraj Singh
articles.full_content:
Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh, today conducted an official inspection of the SRF Limited manufacturing facility situated at the SIPCOT Industrial Park in Gummidipoondi, Tiruvallur district. The facility is engaged in the manufacture of Nylon-6 and Nylon-66, which constitute vital inputs for key industries, including automobile tyres and the defence sector. Tiruvallur District Collector Ms. Kavitha IAS, Member of the Legislative Assembly (Gummidipoondi) Shri Vijayakumar, and senior government officials accompanied the Union Minister during the inspection.
Visiting the various production units of the establishment, the Union Minister reviewed the manufacturing processes and enquired about the range of technical textile products being produced at the plant.
Addressing media representatives following the inspection, Shri Giriraj Singh underscored the pivotal role played by SRF Limited in the domestic production of Nylon-6 and Nylon-66 for strategic sectors such as tyres and defence.
“The Government of India remains steadfastly committed to advancing the growth of the technical textiles sector. Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government has approved a ₹ 10,600 crore Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme to provide a major impetus to technical textiles,” the Union Minister stated.
Reaffirming the Centre’s continued support for the industry, Shri Giriraj Singh assured that the Government will continue to extend all necessary assistance to leading manufacturing establishments to propel India’s technical textiles sector to the next stage of growth.
articles.summary: Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh, today conducted an official inspection of the SRF Limited manufacturing facility situated at the SIPCOT Industrial Park in Gummidipoondi, Tiruvallur district. The facility is engaged in the manufacture of Nylon-6 and Nylon-66, which constitute vital inputs for key industries, including automobile tyres and the defence sector. Kavitha IAS, Member of the Legislative Assembly (Gummidipoondi) Shri Vijayakumar, and senior government officials accompanied the Union Minister during the inspection.

articles.title: Union Minister of Textiles Shri Giriraj Singh Reviews Textile Sector Initiatives in Tamil Nadu; Emphasises Weaver Welfare, Product Diversification and Export Promotion
articles.full_content:
The Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh, undertook a series of official engagements in Tamil Nadu on 23 and 24 November 2026, focusing on strengthening the textile and sericulture sectors, promoting industrial development, enhancing weavers’ livelihoods and boosting textile exports.
On 24 November 2026, the Minister chaired a review meeting in Chennai with senior officials from the Central and State Governments associated with the handloom sector, Central Silk Board, PM MITRA Park and various verticals of the textile industry. Representatives from industry and allied sectors also participated in the meeting.
The meeting was attended by Smt. R. Lilly, IAS, Secretary, Handlooms, Handicrafts, Textiles and Khadi Department, Government of Tamil Nadu; Thiru R. Sadheesh, IAS, Director of Sericulture (Full Additional Charge), Government of Tamil Nadu; Thiru S. A. Raman, IAS, Managing Director, SIPCOT; Tmt. P. Uma Maheswari, IAS, Director of Handlooms, Tamil Nadu; Smt. Swayamprava Pani, Additional Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles; Shri Anil Kumar, IRS, Director (Infrastructure), Ministry of Textiles; and Shri P. Sivakumar, IFS, Member Secretary, Central Silk Board, along with other senior officials from the Ministry and associated organisations.
The discussions focused on reviewing the progress of the "PM MITRA Park at Virudhunagar, Tamil Nadu"; diversification of silk products in Kanchipuram; enhancement of weavers’ income and revenue; promotion of new-age fibres; and the potential for replicating the successful Kanchipuram cluster model in other textile sectors. The Minister also emphasised the need for a focused and coordinated approach towards promoting textile exports and strengthening India's competitiveness in international markets.
Reiterating the Government's commitment to the welfare of the textile sector, Shri Giriraj Singh emphasised the importance of providing better opportunities, improved facilities and necessary support to weavers, artisans and all stakeholders associated with the textile industry across Tamil Nadu, including Chennai.
Earlier, on 23 November 2026, following the inauguration of the 27th International Congress on Sericulture and Silk Industry (ISCC-2026) and the Silk Mark Expo 2026 in Chennai, The Minister visited the "Perarignar Anna Handloom Silk Park, Kanchipuram". He inspected the handloom units and viewed the silk products of Prakash Silks & Sarees. He also interacted with weavers and the Board of Directors to review the progress of the project and understand the facilities and opportunities available to the weaving community. Emphasising the importance of strengthening traditional silk weaving, he highlighted the need for improved infrastructure, better facilities and enhanced market opportunities to increase weavers’ income and take Kanchipuram’s rich silk heritage to greater heights.

Data Users Conference on the New Series of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP) Held in Mumbai on 23 November 2026
articles.full_content:
The The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as the Knowledge Partner, organised a “Data Users Conference on the New Series of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP)” on 23 November 2026 at Mumbai. Following the release of revised series of GDP, CPI and IIP at different points during 2026, the conference was organised to familiarise data users with the methodological changes, data sources and key improvements incorporated in each of the revised series. It also aimed to facilitate a better understanding of these changes and their implications for the resulting estimates.
The conference brought together representatives of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), SEBI, economists, forecasters, credit rating agencies, experts from financial institutions and the banking sector, academia, research institutions, industry and investor organisations, users of official statistics and senior officials of the Central and State Governments. The inaugural session comprised welcome remarks by Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI; the setting of the context by Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI; the inaugural address by Dr. Poonam Gupta, Deputy Governor, RBI; the keynote address by Shri Deepak Parekh, Former Chairman, HDFC; and the vote of thanks by Shri Siddhartha Kundu, ADG, National Accounts Division, MoSPI. A booklet containing brief concept notes on the revised series of these indices was shared with the participants.
Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), in his welcome address, noted that macroeconomic statistics form the foundation of economic analysis, policy making and informed decision making and that GDP, CPI and IIP together provide a comprehensive measure of economic activity and growth. He observed that, as the structure of the economy, production processes, consumption patterns and technology continue to evolve, the statistical system must evolve continuously to remain representative of prevailing economic realities. He recalled that MoSPI had completed the base revision of these three indicators and launched the new series during 2026, with greater use of administrative and survey-based data, wider coverage and important methodological improvements and acknowledged the contribution of expert committees, central ministries, State Governments, RBI and other institutions.
Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, while setting the context, noted that the conference was being held in Mumbai after about a year, this time after the completion of the base revision exercise, with the first-quarter GDP estimates of the new series already released and the second-quarter estimates due shortly. He stated that the two-year exercise had been made possible by the support of several expert committees, other ministries and departments, State Governments, the RBI and other regulatory agencies.
